name: Eternal Limited (formerly Zomato)
period: Q4 FY26 and FY26 (to 31 March 2026), with the Q1 FY27 update
evidence_note: Built from press coverage of the results and from Eternal's own web pages. The company's shareholder letters and annual report were too large to open, so none of this has been checked against a primary document yet.

q1.title: Eternal Q1FY27 shareholders' letter page (headline only)

headline.text: A group of four consumer-internet businesses. Reported revenue is distorted by Blinkit's switch to owning inventory, and food delivery earns almost all the profit.

answers.a: Zomato: restaurant food delivery. Blinkit: groceries and essentials from dark stores, now mainly inventory-led. District: restaurant bookings, movie and event tickets. Hyperpure: supplies to restaurants.

answers.q: Which products contribute most to revenue?
answers.a: By reported revenue, Blinkit was about 70% of FY26 (37,779 of 54,364, from press). By profit, food delivery: Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA 532 against 37 for Blinkit. District lost 81.

Food delivery had 27.2 million average monthly transacting customers in Q1 FY27 (24.9 million in Q3 FY26), about 328 thousand restaurant partners and 555 thousand delivery partners (Q2 FY26; the company page says 600 thousand+). One aggregator cites 109 million unique annual transacting customers across all businesses in FY26.
Mostly B2C: the company reports consumer order value of 31,120 in Q1 FY27 (+54%). Hyperpure is B2B, and restaurants pay commissions and advertising on the consumer app.
Domestic: operations across India, no export revenue. A small going-out expansion into the UAE is mentioned in thin secondary coverage.
Service, platform and trading. Purchases of stock-in-trade were about 61% of Q4 FY26 total expenses (10,687 of 17,406), because Blinkit and Hyperpure hold inventory.
Blinkit's capacity is its stores: 2,443 at Q1 FY27. Order value per store per day was 8.27 lakh against a company steady-state assumption of 11 lakh, about 75% (our division).

capacity.title: Capacity and utilisation: Blinkit stores
capacity.definition: Capacity is the store network. The company's steady-state assumptions give a yardstick for throughput per store.

claims.text: Order value per store per day was 8.27 lakh in Q1 FY27, 13% higher than a year earlier; about 331 million orders in the quarter, average order value 518.

Company steady-state assumptions: order value per store per day 11 lakh, capex per store including warehousing 2.5 crore (up from 1 crore), working capital 12 days of order value, EBIT margin 4% of order value.
At 8.27 lakh against 11 lakh, stores run at about 75% of the steady-state assumption (8.27 divided by 11).

Target of 3,000 stores by March 2027, as stated in the Q3 FY26 letter and repeated by press; sources disagree on the date. Reaching it needs about 557 more stores, at 2.5 crore each about 1,400 crore.

capacity.reading: For Blinkit, capacity is stores and throughput per store against management's own target, not a plant. Food delivery has no fixed capacity: partner supply and restaurant coverage are the limits.

sync.claim: Revenue up 196% in Q4 and 169% in FY26 (54,364 against 20,243).
sync.statutory: Like-for-like growth was about 64% in Q4.
sync.why: The headline is inflated by the move to owning inventory. Growth should be judged on order value or like-for-like.

sync.claim: Blinkit reached positive adjusted EBITDA (37, 0.3% of order value).
sync.statutory: FY26 profit after tax was 366, down from 527.
sync.why: Adjusted and statutory measures differ; adjusted is company-defined.

sync.claim: A strong cash position of 17,972 at Q4 FY26.
sync.statutory: Not checked against the financial statements. At 6 to 7% the cash could earn more than the whole FY26 profit.
sync.why: How much of profit is treasury income needs the annual report.

sync.claim: On track for 3,000 stores by March 2027.
sync.statutory: 2,443 at Q1 FY27; 200 were added in Q1.
sync.why: The target date is reported inconsistently across sources.

guidance.outcome: Raised from 1 crore to 2.5 crore, which makes the earlier assumption look optimistic.

guidance.item: Blinkit order value per store per day of 11 lakh at steady state.

definitions.meaning: The company's order-value measure used for Blinkit and Zomato. The exact definition was not read from a primary document.
Company-defined. They differ from statutory revenue and profit; the reconciliation was not read.

comparability: Blinkit moved from a marketplace to an inventory-led model, so reported revenue now includes the full value of goods sold. Reported FY26 growth (+169%) is not comparable with earlier years.
Hyperpure's reported revenue fell 47% in Q4 because revenue moved into Blinkit; like-for-like it grew 37%.
Sources disagree on whether the change began in Q1 or Q2 of FY26.

risks.text: Blinkit's profit is still close to zero while it adds stores; competition in quick commerce is intense.
A leadership transition was mentioned in coverage of the Q3 FY26 results; details are not verified.

open_questions: Read the Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 shareholder letters and the FY26 annual report to confirm every figure above.
How much of FY26 profit is interest income on the 17,972 of cash?
Blinkit's Q1 FY27 profit is reported as 102 by one outlet and 365 by another. Which measure is which?
Does a customer concentration disclosure exist, and what does the segment note say about geography?
